articles.headline: Original GTA 6 leaker pleads guilty to hacking Rockstar Games, years after first revealing Lucia
keyFacts: The 21-year-old responsible for the 2022 Rockstar Games hack and GTA 6 leaks pleaded guilty to cyber offenses at the Woolwich Crown Court.
The attacks on Rockstar, Uber, and EE/BT caused an estimated £10m in damages, which the defendant committed using an Amazon Fire Stick and a hotel TV.
The leaker, who also hacked developer Slack channels and threatened to release source code, has not yet been sentenced.
body: The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses.

The GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January. On Monday, at the Woolwich Crown Court in South East London, he pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and a number of other companies, including Uber and EE/BT, in cyber attacks estimated to have caused £10m in damages.

At the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from. Somewhat surprisingly, he then managed to hack the multi-billion dollar game maker with nothing but an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel room's TV and a bluetooth-connected keyboard and mouse.

As the BBC reports, he also managed to break into the developer's Slack channels, before threatening to release the GTA 6 source code if Rockstar failed to contact him within the day. The leaker has yet to be sentenced.

Those 2022 leaks were quite substantial, too, revealing about an hour of unfinished gameplay and clueing the world in on Lucia's existence - the series' first female protagonist in years. Of course, those 2022 leaks shouldn't be confused with 2026's, which saw Cyberleek spill nuggets of nearly finished clips onto the internet, despite Rockstar's best efforts to keep GTA 6 a closely guarded secret.

"We recently suffered a network intrusion in which an unauthorised third-party illegally accessed and downloaded confidential information from our systems, including early development footage for the next Grand Theft Auto," Rockstar said at the time, before it had officially unveiled GTA 6. "At this time we do not anticipate any disruption to our live game services, nor any long-term effect on the development of our ongoing projects. We are extremely disappointed to have any details of our next game shared with you all in this way."
Four years later, GTA 6 is finally around the corner - you're probably already aware considering the marketing frenzy Rockstar's been drumming up.

articles.headline: Wyndham Clark engaged to Emily Tanner after teasing proposal plans
keyFacts: Golfer Wyndham Clark announced his engagement to Emily Tanner on Sunday, Nov. 15, in Scottsdale, Arizona.
Clark previously stated his intention to propose following the conclusion of his golf tournament schedule over the summer.
Clark has upcoming international tournaments in Japan and South Africa as part of his post-season schedule.
body: Wydnham Clark followed through on his promise to propose to Emily Tanner after teasing the proposal three months ago.

The two-time U.S. Open champion announced his engagement to Tanner in a joint Instagram post on Sunday, Nov. 15. The couple had a beautiful backdrop of Scottsdale, Arizona, when Clark got down on one knee to ask her to marry him.
She gleefully turned around and put her hand over her mouth in shock before he picked her up and kissed her.
“My forever," the caption read, soundtracked by Noah Kahan's “Orbiter.”
The proposal follows Clark sharing his plans for their future over the summer.

“I’m going to be in Cabo next week,” Clark told reporters on Aug. 25, following the BMW Championship and Tour Championship. “That’s my happy place. So I’ll be down there having fun. Presidents Cup, I’m playing a tournament in Japan.”
“Hopefully get engaged and then going to South Africa for a tournament as well,” he added, “Hopefully, she says yes.”

Tanner has been on the green with Clark and cheering him on from the sidelines as he continues adding more titles to his name. She caddied for him during the Par 3 Contest at the 2026 Masters Tournament at Augusta National Golf Club, and he shared how proud he was to have her by his side.
"Par 3 with my good luck charm," he wrote in the caption.
During a Q&A on Instagram Stories in July, she shared how the couple got together.
“Online/mutual friends," she responded to a fan. We met end of January and fell pretty fast. We’re super similar and get along so so well."
Amid wedding planning, Clark has an upcoming international tournament in Japan as part of his post-season schedule. He will then travel to South Africa for another tournament overseas.

articles.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo’s mum delighted by Portugal’s defeat as boss Jorge Jesus fires back
keyFacts: Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother Dolores Aveiro said she was happy that Denmark defeated Portugal 4-1 in the Nations League.
Aveiro stated that the national team and teammates did not respect Ronaldo, criticizing their handling of his international retirement.
Portugal manager Jorge Jesus said he respects Aveiro and understands her comments ahead of the team's match against Wales.
body: Cristiano Ronaldo’s mum has taken aim at Portugal’s handling of his international retirement – insisting she was ‘happy’ Denmark beat them.
Dolores Aveiro admitted it was ‘well deserved’ to see the national team lose their first match since the five-time Ballon d’Or winner announced his decision .
Ronaldo’s mum said she was ‘happy’ to see Portugal lose to Denmark Instagram @cristiano
Portugal were thrashed 4-1 by Denmark in the Nations League on Saturday – their heaviest ever home loss in a competitive fixture.
Speaking after the match, Aveiro quipped: “The defeat was well deserved, and I was happy about it.”
Ronaldo’s Portugal feud
It came after Ronaldo ended his illustrious international career, which ended with a record 146 goals in 234 caps for his country.
However, his exit came after a public falling out with manager Jorge Jesus during the previous international break.
Ronaldo left the camp early claiming Jesus had broken a promise to play him in a match against Norway.
The 41-year-old was subsequently left as an unused substitute, prompting his unauthorised departure from the squad.
He was later fined €255 and suspended for 30 days, with Jesus reportedly planning to hand him a call-up this month before his retirement.
Portugal’s first outing since that announcement came against Denmark in Braga.
As part of their tribute to Ronaldo, the national team announced they had changed the design of the No.7 on their jerseys.
Ronaldo had worn the iconic shirt number for his country for almost two decades.
Ronaldo retired from international duty after his public spat with Jesus EPA
However, Aveiro was left unsatisfied with the tributes, adding: “The tribute should have been paid in his presence.”
Instead, she has revealed Ronaldo will be honoured by his boyhood club Sporting Lisbon.
She explained: “It’s here, at Sporting, that we’re going to pay tribute to him. Here, they recognise his worth.”
Aveiro continued: “With the national team, he was not respected, not even by his team-mates.”
How did Jorge Jesus respond to Ronaldo’s mum?
Jesus, who won the Saudi Pro League with Ronaldo at Al Nassr last season, has now given his own response to her explosive remarks.
Speaking ahead of Tuesday’s clash with Wales, he said: “Now do I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother? My mother too.
Jesus’ side are preparing to respond against Wales on Tuesday Getty
“Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother is a lady I respect greatly. A mother is still a mother, there’s nothing you can do about it. I understand her statements.”
Despite the defeat to Denmark, Portugal are already into the Nations League quarter-finals.
A draw with Wales in their final match will be enough to ensure progression as group winners.
The two sides meet at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, with kick-off at 7.45pm.

articles.headline: United States v Canada: women’s ice hockey world championship 2026 final – live
keyFacts: The United States and Canada are playing in the 2026 women’s ice hockey world championship final in Herning, Denmark.
Sweden defeated Finland 2-1 in a shootout to win the third-place bronze medal earlier in the day.
The United States entered the final as defending champions seeking their 12th world title while Canada pursued their 14th.
body: A second penalty on the United States. It’s going to be two minutes for holding on Pannek as Wroblewski throws his arms up in disbelief after having a look at the replay. It’s another chance for Canada’s tournament-best power play, a unit that entered today’s game converting at 43%.
Hilary Knight pounces on a rebound in front of goal to draw the Americans level, sending chants of “U-S-A!” ringing around the arena in Herning.
Laila Edwards makes a lovely move at the point to create the opening, with Tessa Janecke also picking up an assist as Knight buries the loose puck past Ann-Renée Desbiens.
It’s Knight’s eighth goal and 11th point of the tournament, and the United States are back on level terms with less than four minutes remaining in the opening period.
Canada have the lead through Sarah Fillier – the second coming of Marie-Philip Poulin? – but the Americans are beginning to turn the screw in the attacking zone.
Kelly Pannek tests Desbiens with a sharp-angle effort from close range, only for the Canadian goaltender to turn it away.
The shots are level at 6-6 with just over five minutes remaining in the opening period.

Canada strike first! Sarah Fillier redirects the puck past Aerin Frankel with a deft backhand finish to give the Canadians the lead midway through the opening period. Jessie Eldridge and Rosalie Tremblay pick up the assists.
That’s five goals in five games for Fillier, who missed Canada’s first two matches through injury but has scored in every appearance since.
And for the first time at this world championship, the United States find themselves trailing.

Canada are enjoying more time in the attacking zone as we reach the first media timeout. Jessie Eldridge goes down under pressure in the American zone, while Caroline Harvey loses her stick in the scramble, but there’s no penalty.
Canada have their first good look at goal as Jessie Eldridge carries the puck into the American zone and sends a backhander toward the net. Frankel corrals it comfortably.
At the other end, Laila Edwards unleashes a blistering shot from the point through traffic, but Desbiens tracks the puck all the way and makes the save.
Both goaltenders have been called into action in a lively opening four minutes.
The lineups are confirmed for tonight’s gold-medal game, with Aerin Frankel in goal for the United States and Ann-Renée Desbiens between the pipes for Canada.

US captain Hilary Knight starts alongside forwards Tessa Janecke and Alex Carpenter, with Megan Keller and Laila Edwards the starting defensive pair. Frankel enters the final having set American records for career wins and shutouts at the women’s world championship.

Canada captain Laura Stacey starts up front with Caitlin Kraemer and Daryl Watts, while Renata Fast and Nicole Gosling form the starting defensive pair. Desbiens has been similarly impressive throughout the tournament, conceding just one goal in three starts.
Today’s gold-medal game will be the 201st meeting between the US and Canada in women’s international hockey, a rivalry stretching back to the inaugural world championship final in 1990.

Canada hold the historical advantage, with 109 victories to the Americans’ 90, plus one tie across the first 200 encounters. But the US have enjoyed the upper hand recently, winning the 2025 world championship final and February’s Olympic gold-medal game, both in overtime.

There is another historical wrinkle to today’s showdown: the last time the women’s worlds were staged in Herning, in 2022, Canada beat the US 2-1 in the final. Brianne Jenner scored twice in just 83 seconds during the second period to secure Canada’s 12th world title.
Four years later, the Canadians return to the same city chasing their 14th. The Americans, meanwhile, are looking to close the gap with a 12th championship of their own.

A fit and firing Sarah Fillier is a welcome sight for Canadian fans. The 26-year-old forward missed the first two games of this world championship with an upper-body injury. Since returning, the forward has wasted little time making her presence felt.

Fillier has scored in all four games she has played, including Sunday’s semi-final against Sweden, when she broke a scoreless deadlock with a power-play goal midway through the second period. Sarah Wozniewicz and Emma Maltais added further goals as Canada completed a 3-0 victory.

The 2022 Beijing Olympic champion, who plays for the PWHL’s New York Sirens, has emerged as one of Canada’s most important attacking players. Her scoring touch could prove crucial against a US defense that has conceded only twice in six games.
US goaltender Aerin Frankel has been quietly making history of her own at this world championship, for all the attention lavished on Americans’ headline-grabbing attack,

Frankel recorded her eighth career shutout at the women’s worlds with a 17-save performance in Sunday’s 5-0 semi-final victory over Finland, breaking the American record previously held by Nicole Hensley.
The Boston Fleet goaltender also became the United States’ all-time leader in world championship victories earlier in the tournament, taking her career tally to 19.

With the Americans having conceded just two goals in six games on their way to tonight’s final, Frankel will face a considerably sterner examination against Canada as the US pursue a 12th world title.
Sweden won the third-place game earlier today, beating Finland 2-1 in a shootout to claim their first medal at the tournament in nearly two decades.

Lina Ljungblom, a forward with the PWHL’s Montréal Victoire, forced overtime with a power-play goal six minutes from the end of regulation after Vancouver Goldeneyes forward Michelle Karvinen had put Finland ahead late in the second period. Hilda Svensson, a 20-year-old Ohio State sophomore, assisted on the equalizer before scoring the decisive shootout goal.
Swedish goaltender Ebba Svensson Traff turned back 29 shots through overtime and stopped four of five shootout attempts. Finland’s Sanni Ahola, of the Ottawa Charge, finished with 35 saves.
It is Sweden’s third world championship bronze, following medals in 2005 and 2007.

If Canada are to halt the Americans’ winning streak, Ann-Renée Desbiens may have to be at her very best. The 32-year-old goaltender has been close to unbeatable in Denmark, allowing just one goal in three starts while posting a tournament-leading .981 save percentage.

Sunday’s 13-save shutout against Sweden was her second in succession and the 10th of her world championship career, leaving her three behind compatriot Kim St-Pierre’s all-time record. It was also her 25th victory at the worlds, extending her own Canadian record.

Desbiens arrives on the back of an outstanding professional season with the Montréal Victoire, whom she helped to their first Walter Cup championship after leading the PWHL with 19 wins and a 1.11 goals-against average.
Against an American attack averaging more than eight goals per game, Canada will need every bit of that form.

Hej, Guardian-læsere and welcome to our live coverage of the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship final between the US and Canada. The fiercest rivalry in women’s hockey is renewed tonight in Herning, Denmark, with another world title on the line, less than nine months after the Americans broke Canadian hearts in the Olympic final at Milano Cortina.

The neighboring countries that share the world’s longest international border have exercised an extraordinary duopoly over this competition since its inception in 1990, combining to win all 24 previous editions. Canada lead the all-time count with 13 titles to the US’s 11, but the balance of power has shifted south of the border in recent years. The Americans are defending world champions after a dramatic 4-3 overtime victory in last year’s final in the Czech Republic, and followed that with a 2-1 overtime win over Canada for Olympic gold in February, sealed by Megan Keller’s winner.

The US arrive in flying form. John Wroblewski’s team have won 20 consecutive games in international competition since their defeat to Canada in the 2024 world championship final, including six straight victories at this tournament by a combined score of 50-2. Sunday’s 5-0 semi-final demolition of Finland followed an even more emphatic 14-0 quarter-final rout of hosts Denmark. Canada, meanwhile, booked their place with a 3-0 shutout of Sweden, behind goals from Sarah Fillier, Sarah Wozniewicz and Emma Maltais.

There have been individual milestones aplenty for the Americans. Caroline Harvey, the 24-year-old defender, has racked up 15 points in six games, a single-tournament record for a player at her position. Taylor Fox has equaled the tournament record with 12 assists, while captain Hilary Knight, now 37 and the US team’s north star for so many years, continues to extend her extraordinary world championship records: 74 goals and 130 points in 93 appearances. Between the pipes, Aerin Frankel recorded her eighth career shutout at the worlds against Finland, another American record.

Yet for all their dominance against the rest of the field, the Americans know Canada represent an altogether different challenge. These familiar opponents have met in 23 of the previous 24 world championship finals, and their last two major title encounters have required overtime to separate them.

Puck drop is scheduled for 1pm ET (7pm local time), with live television coverage on NHL Network in the United States and TSN and RDS in Canada. Canadian viewers can also stream the game on TSN’s digital platforms. We’ll have all the buildup, team news and live updates from Herning right here.

articles.headline: John Mulaney’s SNL Sister Eldercare Ad Is an Instant, Painful Classic
keyFacts: Saturday Night Live aired a parody commercial starring host John Mulaney about female siblings taking on unpaid eldercare duties.
Some viewers on Reddit said the sketch accurately reflected their real-life experiences with uneven family eldercare responsibilities.
Tech companies are exploring artificial intelligence and companion robots as options to assist elderly adults with caregiving needs.
body: Did SNL just add another legendary fake commercial to the show’s hall of fame? On Saturday night, host John Mulaney and the cast delivered a winning pretaped parody commercial that hit a nerve in more than a few households.

In the ad, Mulaney and others fret about their aging parents. Nursing homes don’t appeal, yet in-home care would cost too much. Fortunately, Mulaney has heard about Sister, “a live-in, 24/7 eldercare provider that is completely free, and also your sister.”

“I love my mom more than anything,” says another adult son, played by Andrew Dismukes. “That doesn’t mean I want to help her in the bathroom. Sister doesn’t either. But she will, whereas I won’t. That’s the Sister difference!”

Jane Wickline plays a frantic sister who drops everything, quits her job, breaks her lease, and moves halfway across the country to take care of her elderly dad (Tommy Brennan, ironically one of the youngest cast members).
Mulaney says he just had to text his sister, “Dad fell,” and voilà, she instantly appeared.
Mikey Day plays a doctor who, as the author of the astutely named book Not It! A Son’s Guide to Elder Care, explains how it works.

“Years of internalized sexism warps Sister’s brain into thinking caretaking is her responsibility, and somehow, not yours,” Day says. “Next, your text arrives, instantly activating her. And that’s it! You’re done for life! See you at the funeral!”

Anyone who’s ever had to care for elderly parents can relate to Sister’s duties: Making those torturous, endless calls to doctors, insurance companies and pharmacists, all while screaming, “Speak to human!” at unhelpful phone trees.

Meanwhile, Kenan Thompson rejoices that he’s still in the will despite doing nothing, and Mulaney and Brennan bond over griping about Sister’s diet restrictions. Mulaney urges viewers to sign up now for the free addition of Sister’s Husband, who just doesn’t know why this burden has to fall on his (defensive) wife.
A quickly flashed line at the end of the ad notes, “Offer void if Sister has a good therapist,” who’d presumably tell her to insist her brothers do their share.
It wasn’t just a fictional sketch to some SNL viewers on Reddit.
“This isn’t funny, this is life for a lot of women,” wrote one person.
“I watched this skit earlier today with my husband, and I started crying,” said another. “It’s exactly the situation I’m in while my brother travels the world.”

The point of the ad is that the duties fell on one very human family member. But tech companies are increasingly eyeing that responsibility as an opportunity for AI or robotic help — if that’s something you and your family are willing to try.

One device we’ve seen is a companion robot, ElliQ, that’s meant to live with elderly family members and serve as a digital assistant, social companion and health advocate. (We tried it out with some of our parents and grandparents.) And a 2025 University of Michigan survey found that older adults often find AI smart home devices and voice assistants useful in helping them age in place. CNET also has a roundup of the most reliable smart tech to help people age in place.

No robot or AI can replace the personal touch and self-sacrificial dedication of Sister. I haven’t replayed an SNL parody commercial this many times since the now-classic 2017 ad for Alexa Echo Silver: For the Greatest Generation.
And yes, I texted the Sister ad to my two sisters (but not my brothers).

body: Arion Kurtaj, the then-17-year-old hacker who allegedly leaked early Grand Theft Auto 6 footage back in 2022 after hacking into developer Rockstarâs servers, has officially pled guilty to the crime four years later.

The BBC reports that the now-21-year-old pled guilty at the Woolwich Crown Court in London today, November 16, both to the Rockstar hack that leaked early in-development footage of GTA 6, and to several other cybercrimes carried out as part of the hacking gang Lapsus$. The entire saga has been wild to watch unfold. Kurtaj first hacked into Rockstar’s servers while on bail for other crimes, and was able to do so with an Amazon Fire Stick in a hotel room while under police protection. He then posted in the companyâs Slack threatening the company if it didnât negotiate with him over Telegram. He pled not guilty in 2022.

Initially, Kurtaj was deemed unfit to stand trial, with medical professionals citing his acute autism as cause to have him instead sentenced to life in a hospital prison. However, in January 2026 it was determined he was now fit to stand trial, and he subsequently pled guilty. His sentencing will be scheduled for a later date.

Rockstar refused to negotiate with Kurtaj at the time, but the studio has acknowledged the entire thing over the years, with Grand Theft Auto 6âs second trailer containing what seems to be a joke poking fun at the hack asÂ the gameâs co-lead Jason says that heâs âfixing some leaksâ while patching up a roof. articles.headline: NoisyTCP bug gives Linux servers a remote crash problem 11 years in the making
keyFacts: Security researcher Hyunwoo Kim discovered NoisyTCP, a Linux kernel vulnerability allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to crash entire servers.
The flaw affects almost all Linux distributions since 2015 and can take down host machines running containerized applications or virtual machines.
A fix was committed to the upstream Linux kernel on November 3, requiring administrators to update their distribution kernels.
body: The researcher who sounded the alarm over Dirty Frag earlier this year has uncovered another Linux kernel flaw, and this one lets attackers crash entire servers remotely without so much as a password.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-99288 and dubbed NoisyTCP, was discovered by security researcher Hyunwoo Kim , who says it affects almost all Linux distributions. The flaw dates back to October 2015 and went unnoticed until this year, when Kim found and patched it.

Attackers don't need to log in or get their hands on any credentials to cause trouble. They can simply knock the server over, although there's no evidence yet that the flaw can be used to steal data or hijack a machine.

The bug is buried in Linux's TCP networking code. Two parts of the kernel can trip over each other while processing incoming traffic, leaving one trying to use memory that's already been freed. When that happens, Linux can panic and take the whole machine down with it.

Kim says there's no need for any special server configuration either. Services such as Nginx, Apache, and SSH can be vulnerable straight out of the box. An attacker needs access to an open TCP port on a system that processes incoming network traffic across multiple receive queues or CPUs.

Perhaps more concerning for administrators running containerized workloads, the damage isn't necessarily limited to the application being attacked. Because the flaw sits in the Linux kernel, crashing a web server inside a container can take down the underlying host and anything else running on it.

Kim found that the attack was particularly effective against virtual machines. During testing, he managed to crash Nginx, Apache, and SSH servers running on QEMU/KVM virtual machines in between five seconds and two minutes.
Physical hardware put up more of a fight. Even after tailoring his exploit to the target machine, Kim needed roughly 14 hours to crash a bare-metal server running Nginx.

Kim has a knack for finding holes in Linux. Back in May, he uncovered Dirty Frag , a kernel bug that allowed local users to gain root privileges. That one caused headaches for administrators when a working exploit went public before patches were ready.

His latest discovery, NoisyTCP, has another potentially nasty trick up its sleeve. Kim identified a second exploitation path involving a use-after-free condition, although pulling it off is considerably more difficult than simply crashing a server.

In his advisory, Kim says he has developed a limited exploit targeting virtual machines in a lab environment but has yet to demonstrate a general-purpose remote code execution attack. For the moment, the confirmed impact is remote denial of service.

A fix was committed to the upstream Linux kernel on November 3, but administrators will need to check whether their distribution has shipped an updated kernel. Red Hat has rated the vulnerability Important , assigning it a CVSS score of 7.5.
For those unable to patch immediately, Kim suggests two temporary workarounds: disabling TCP SYN cookies or restricting incoming packet processing to a single receive queue.

Neither is particularly appealing. Disabling SYN cookies reduces protection against SYN flood attacks, while limiting packet processing can hurt network performance. The former also needs to be applied separately to containers using their own network namespaces.

Kim published the details on November 15, once the disclosure embargo was lifted. The bug had been hiding in plain sight since 2015, leaving Linux servers vulnerable to remote crashes for 11 years. Not bad for a flaw that doesn't even require a login. ®

articles.headline: Tesla goes all-in on the Cybercab with upcoming €3B Berlin Gigafactory expansion
keyFacts: Tesla announced a €3 billion expansion of its Berlin gigafactory to produce autonomous Cybercab vehicles.
Construction will start in 2027 to begin Cybercab production in 2029, Tesla manufacturing director André Thierig said.
Tesla plans to end Cybertruck production next year to dedicate more resources toward its Cybercab project.
body: Just two months after putting its first Cybercabs on the road, Tesla is making a multibillion-dollar bet on mass production of the golden-hued, two-seat autonomous vehicles.

The company announced Monday that it will spend €3 billion ($3.3 billion) to expand its Berlin gigafactory, with plans to begin building Cybercabs there in 2029. The new building in Grünheide, just east of Berlin, will be capable of producing up to 1 million vehicles per year, André Thierig, Tesla’s senior director of manufacturing for the site, wrote on LinkedIn.
Construction is expected to begin in the first half of 2027. The expansion will make the facility the most technologically advanced of all Tesla factories, Thierig added.
Tesla has been directing more resources toward the Cybercab project, a reflection of its mission to become an AI and robotics company, rather than just an automaker.
The company has already announced plans to cease production of the Cybertruck next year, in part to make room for Cybercab manufacturing at its factory in Austin, Texas.

Musk doesn’t see much of a future for drive-it-yourself EVs even though demand for the Model 3 and Model Y has remained strong despite flagging U.S. sales. The company delivered more than 486,000 vehicles in the third quarter, about 6,000 more than the second quarter. Sales in Europe have been rising as EV adoption continues apace.

Musk has been far more interested in pushing the company toward fully automated driving systems that don’t require a human driver to pay attention — unlike the company’s current advanced driver assistance system, known as Full Self-Driving (Supervised).

The steering wheel-free Cybercab, which was first revealed in 2024 and launched publicly in September, is the current centerpiece of that plan. It’s notable not just for its lack of a steering wheel, pedals, and other traditional motor vehicle equipment, some of which is required under federal safety standards. (Federal regulators are currently investigating Tesla’s self-certification of the vehicle.)

Tesla’s approach to self-driving systems differs from that of competitors such as Waymo. Tesla relies solely on cameras, rather than additional other sensors such as lidar, to help its self-driving system the means to understand its environment. Camera data mimics human vision, but without sufficient training, AI models can struggle to interpret situations that additional sensor data might help clarify.

Tesla has so far taken a slow approach to its Cybercab rollout. The vehicles have been restricted from driving late at night, though Tesla has been working to extend their operating hours. In the more than two months that Cybercabs have been operating, they haven’t had any major incidents.

That track record appears to have given Tesla enough confidence to commit significant resources to expanding Cybercab production and availability. Tesla has about 1,307 robotaxis registered in Texas. Most are modified Model Y vehicles that are used in robotaxi services in several Texas cities. But the Cybercab numbers are growing with about 573 on roads in Austin and soon Dallas.
Now, Europe is firmly on its roadmap, too.

A broadcast showed the American in conversation with her coach Mark Knowles, calling the 19-year-old a "diva" and saying she has lost respect for Andreeva's coach Conchita Martinez for not calling out her behaviour.
"Someone actually asked me if we planned it or did it on purpose to draw attention to the event," Camillo told Sky Sports' lead tennis commentator, Jonathan Overend.

"I wish that we were so crafty and strategic but we can't put ourselves in any situation where we put our athletes at risk. Our number one objective as a member services organisation for our players is to protect our players.

"What Jess said is competitive banter. I don't think there was anything particularly salacious in it. But having mics lying around that aren't being properly managed is not how the WTA expects to execute and operate.
"It created a viral moment. It created a lot of dialogue. But that's not intentional and not something you should expect to see us doing in the future.

"I've had this conversation here that I come from a variety of different sports. Before joining the WTA, I exclusively worked in male sports. I worked at the NBA and majorly baseball and it's quite common for there to be competitive banter that is brought into the forefront.
"It's up to the athletes for what they feel comfortable with and what they don't. But a little drama isn't bad for ticket sales.
"It's not bad for viewership. It's not bad for commentary. That's just a reality."
Andreeva laughed off the hot mic moment and went on to defeat Pegula 6-3 6-4 on Saturday, in a match that gained an extra layer of intrigue to reach the WTA Finals title match.
She concluded a stunning week with a second victory over Elina Svitolina to win the season-ending tournament.
WTA finances and maximising financial opportunity
The WTA was forced to replace the venue for the season-ending event from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in July, which represented a major financial setback for the governing body.

The deal with the Saudi Tennis Federation (STF) included record prize money over a three-year period, but the ongoing tension between Iran and the United States made planning for the Finals more challenging, eventually forcing the tournament to move to Indian Wells in California.

The body is projecting operating losses of £17.3m ($23m) for 2026 and expects to hold roughly £11.3m ($15m) in cash by the end of the year, according to The Telegraph. Camillo remains confident of finding extra revenue streams through in-house media rights and sponsorship growth to create financial stability.

"Our ambition for the WTA Finals is equal prize money [with the men's tour]. That's our ambition, just as we expected of the Grand Slams. All of our combined 1000 events will have equal prize money in 2027," she said.

"We've been building fandom. We've been operating globally. We've been creating superstar athletes through our platform for many, many decades, and so the athletes have the opportunity not to just earn on the court, but also to control their own brands and monetise that off the court.

"WTA intends to remain in its position as number one in the hearts and minds of fans, in the mindset and investment of our sponsors, and we want to be building an even greater platform on which our great athletes can compete, not only one that they can enjoy from the ferocity of the crowd, but also one that enables them to maximise their financial opportunity to the best of our ability."
WTA intends to have 'better controls' of revenue streams
One of the WTA revenue streams comes from selling data, match data, court feeds to data companies with the betting industry a large part of that.
British tennis star Jodie Burrage called on social media platforms to hold people accountable for sending death threats and abuse.
Burrage, who was playing her first WTA Tour match since Wimbledon last summer, received death threats and online abuse following a first-round defeat at a tournament in India.
The 27-year-old shared a raft of abusive messages sent to her Instagram account. Alongside the video, Burrage wrote: "Nice welcome back to the tour. I remember why I left."

Camillo said: "The complexity of official data to these partners is sort of an industry inside thing. But the reality is that through having official partnerships, you actually can have more integrity and controls.

"If you don't have relationships with these variety of platforms, you can turn into a little bit of the wild, wild west. It's not to say that there isn't a financial element to these relationships. That would be disingenuous. Of course there is. But it does also enable us to have a partnership that leads to better controls."

articles.headline: Five-try Joseph set to start for England against All Blacks
keyFacts: Will Joseph is expected to start for England against New Zealand after scoring five tries in a victory over Japan.
Joseph secured his spot on the wing due to an ankle injury sidelining Immanuel Feyi-Waboso for the autumn matches.
England will play New Zealand on Saturday, 21 November, at Allianz Stadium in the Nations Championship.
body: - Published
England's Will Joseph is in line to retain his place for Saturday's blockbuster Nations Championship meeting with New Zealand after scoring five tries against Japan.
In the absence of the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Joseph is understood to be in pole position to reprise his role on the wing after a performance packed with pace and finishing ability.
Joseph scored a hat-trick inside the first 19 minutes, on the way to becoming only the fifth England men's player to score five tries in one match.
He also headed the team's charts for metres carried (224) and top speed (21.7mph).
The 24-year-old won his second Test cap in Saturday's 78-15 thrashing of the Brave Blossoms, four and half years after making his debut as a teenager.

After a late cameo as a replacement in England's second Test win over Australia in July 2022, Joseph struggled to fulfil his promise. Boyhood club London Irish went into liquidation and a stint at Harlequins was hampered by injury and a lack of game time.

However, Joseph has been a key part of Gloucester's resurgence this season and, watched by elder brother and former England centre Jonathan Joseph, he made a sensational return to international rugby at Allianz Stadium last weekend.

"He is just so fast. He doesn't look too fast in the first two steps and then he is just gone. He gets away from people," said former England wing Chris Ashton on BBC Radio 5 Live of Joseph's ability.
"He floats, doesn't he?" added England team-mate Ben Earl to BBC Sport.
"The way he carries himself, he does really move like his brother. They are so, so similar."

With Feyi-Waboso ruled out of the autumn by an ankle injury, Cadan Murley is the other specialist wing in England's squad vying with Joseph for a spot alongside likely first-choice Tommy Freeman in the back three.

After victories over Australia and Japan this autumn, England are second in the Nations Championship northern hemisphere standings and in line for a play-off meeting with South Africa on finals weekend on 27-29 November.
However, that could change considerably, with New Zealand leading the southern hemisphere table and second-place South Africa taking on Ireland, who are behind England only on points difference.

articles.headline: Fed is modeling how the AI boom could change the economy
keyFacts: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said the central bank is developing models to evaluate how artificial intelligence could impact the economy.
Warsh stated potential AI scenarios range from broad economic gains to labor market disruptions and displaced jobs.
Recent economic reports showed rising October inflation and 165,000 added jobs, raising odds of a Fed interest rate hike.
body: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said Monday that the Fed is developing models for how artificial intelligence might shape the labor market in the coming years.

Warsh, speaking at the Productivity and Jobs Task Force Conference in San Francisco, said the central bank is examining an array of potential outcomes from the boom in AI, which the Trump administration has branded as “super intelligence,” or SI, rather than AI.
HUGE GOP ELECTION LOSSES SPUR DEBATES ABOUT POPULIST ECONOMICS

“It’s worth considering the range of economic outcomes we could see over the next several years, depending on how SI progresses,” Warsh said in prepared remarks. “The board’s staff has begun to evaluate various contingencies, applying stylized, model-based frameworks to generate scenarios.”

There have been major questions about exactly how AI will shape not only the stock market, but also the broader economy and labor markets . Some think that AI could be a very big net positive, driving growth while unemployment stays low, while other economists highlight the notion that the boom could end up costing jobs .

Warsh said that, at one end of the modeling, AI could lead to increased productivity and economic gains “that are shared broadly across labor and the owners of capital.” In that scenario, he said real GDP would rise above its long-run average while unemployment remains low.
But he said other outcomes are less ideal for the labor market.

“An SI-driven expansion could bring substantial labor market disruption as some jobs are displaced, rather than complemented, by technology,” Warsh said. “GDP growth would still rise above its long-term average. But widespread automation, combined with labor market frictions, could push the jobless rate above levels consistent with full employment.”

The chairman also said that AI could disappoint and that, after the recent investment boom, stock gains could move in the other direction, leading to an economic slowdown as well as an increase in unemployment.
“In time, the economy would recover, but without the productivity gains,” Warsh said.
AI has been a hot topic in recent years as the technology has grown in usage and integration throughout the economy. Many economists point to AI as driving recent gains in the stock market.
The benchmark S&P 500 has risen more than 8.7% in 2026 alone and even more over the past calendar year.
Meanwhile, the tech-heavy Nasdaq has also grown since the start of the year and over the past 12 months.

Notably, the speech from Warsh comes just days after two hot inflation reports raised the odds of the Fed increasing interest rates at its next meeting. Warsh didn’t address interest rate policy in the Monday speech.
The country’s most closely watched inflation report, the consumer price index, showed prices rose sharply by 0.4% in October.

Because of the government shutdown in October 2025, the Bureau of Labor Statistics did not publish how much inflation increased on a 12-month basis, although economists estimate that the annual number is somewhere in the high 3% to low 4% range — well above the central bank’s 2% target. That reading was higher than forecasters had expected.
Inflation, as measured by the producer price index, rose two-tenths of a percentage point to 6.5% for the year ending in October, the BLS then reported on Friday.
And while the PPI reading was slightly better than expected, that 6.5% climb marked the biggest annual gain since November 2022 under then-President Joe Biden and then-Fed Chairman Jerome Powell.
POST-ELECTION ECONOMIC REPORTS MAKE FED INTEREST RATE HIKE ALL BUT CERTAIN
It is also worth noting that the country’s labor market has been more resilient than expected.

The economy added 165,000 new payroll jobs in October, the Bureau of Labor Statistics recently reported — many more than expected. Also, the unemployment rate fell one-tenth of a percentage point to 4.1%.

articles.headline: You won't find Nothing phones at US carriers, but here's how you can still buy them
keyFacts: In June 2026, Nothing partnered with Best Buy to sell its Android phones and audio gadgets in over 500 US stores.
Nothing lacks deals with major US carriers like Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile, requiring customers to purchase unlocked devices.
Nothing plans to launch a flagship store in New York City in the near future.
body: You won't find Nothing phones at US carriers, but here's how you can still buy them
While you can't get one at an AT&T or Verizon store, Nothing has partnered with Best Buy.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Nothing is bringing its latest Android smartphone to the US market, hoping that a minimalist aesthetic, strong camera and a low price entice American buyers away from Apple, Samsung and Google. Technically advanced for an entry-level phone, the Nothing Phone 4a Pro made waves when it was released in March 2026 alongside the company's latest line of headphones. Despite the excitement, spurred by a slick new design and a marketing campaign headlined by brand ambassador and shareholder Charli XCX, Americans have had trouble getting their hands on the cyberpunk smartphone.

Nothing's lack of American market penetration can be chalked up to a variety of factors. For one thing, the startup relied on a beta-program to sell and test its Phone 3a, Phone 3a Pro, and CMF Phone 2 Pro stateside. Moreover, the London company has yet to open a brick and mortar shop in the continental US, although it plans to launch a flagship store in New York City in the near future. This lack of visibility in American storefronts makes it difficult for shoppers of unlocked cellphones to directly compare the startup's offerings with its competitors. And although the firm states that its American online sales are on the rise, its yet to experience a breakthrough.

The greatest hurdle, however, may be Nothing's approach to phone carrier partnerships. To date, the company has yet to strike a deal with American carriers like Verizon, AT&T or T-Mobile. This is an acute challenge for American buyers, since most purchase their phone through their carriers. However, this doesn't mean that getting your hands on the startup's new smartphone, the Nothing Phone 4a Pro, is impossible.
Getting your hands on a Nothing phone

In June 2026, Nothing struck a deal with Best Buy to bring its Android phones and audio gadgets to more than 500 stores across the country. For those not within spitting distance of these select Best Buy locales, you can find the company's phones, headphones and earbuds on Best Buy's website.

Prior to its deal with Best Buy, you could only purchase Nothing's products online, either through the company's Amazon store or its official website. But thanks British company's first brick and mortar retail deal in the US, you can now walk into an American storefront and try a Nothing phone for yourself. The move could be a major boon for the startup, allowing potential customers to directly compare Nothing's cyberpunk aesthetics to its competitors. And although Nothing's US sales grew steadily over the past calendar year, the latest venture into storefronts could further establish the chic minimalist startup on the American phone scene.

As it stands, Nothing offers two smartphones to American audiences: the Nothing Phone 4a Pro and Nothing Phone 3. The former, released earlier in June 2026, is an affordable midrange smartphone with a bold design, strong battery life, a decent camera and an updated version of the company's popular Glyph Matrix. The Nothing Phone 3, meanwhile, is a more powerful phone built for an AI-heavy experience. Powered by Snapdragon's 8s Gen 4 processor, it delivered a significant performance jump from Nothing's previous models. However, it is also significantly more expensive. Crowned as the company's "first flagship" phone, it is an enticing option facing stiff competition.
Finding the right carrier

Nothing's bring your own device (BYOD) approach is great for those seeking flexible, budget friendly carrier options. Although not available to purchase through an existing carrier, Nothing gives buyers the flexibility to choose the network that is best for them.

One strong option would be signing up with a mobile virtual network operator, or MVNO, which lease access to larger carriers' networks like AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile for a cheaper price point. Plans with MVNOs like Mint Mobile, US Mobile and Google Fi offer affordable plans that you can easily connect to your new minimalist smartphone.

Those looking for the reliability of a major carrier can opt to sign up for a plan with AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon. However, some plans are more difficult to setup than others. For one thing, the Nothing Phone 4a Pro's Amazon page warns against linking the unlocked phone with any of Verizon's networks. Of course, linking a Nothing phone to a Verizon it isn't impossible, just inconvenient. To do so, Verizon must manually add your phone's IMEI number to its database. According to some reviews, customers found the process of doing so difficult. Notably, Nothing doesn't guarantee full network performance on Verizon's networks.

To avoid the hassle, you can limit your search to T-Mobile, AT&T and MNVOs utilizing their mobile networks. For more information on Nothing's US compatibility metrics, visit the company's support page.

articles.headline: Uber data breach sees hackers steal license information on thousands of drivers
keyFacts: Uber disclosed that sensitive driver data was exposed following a hack of third-party service provider Fireworks AI.
TechCrunch reported that the stolen data included driver's license information for thousands of Uber drivers across multiple states.
Uber and Fireworks are notifying affected users, with Uber offering free identity theft and credit monitoring services.
body: - Uber discloses third-party breach that exposed driver data, including driver’s license information for thousands of individuals
- The incident stemmed from a compromise at AI infrastructure provider Fireworks, which was also targeted in broader LLMjacking attacks
- Uber is notifying affected users and offering identity theft and credit monitoring services while investigations continue
Popular ride-hailing service Uber has confirmed it lost sensitive data after one of its third-party service providers was hacked.
The company filed a new notice with multiple US Attorney General’s Offices and shared a copy of the letter it is now sending out to affected individuals.
In the letter, it says that a threat actor got ahold of login credentials belonging to an employee of the service and used them to pull Uber’s data.
Driver’s licenses and other data
The letter does not disclose key details, like the nature of the data that was stolen, or how many people were affected.

According to TechCrunch, however, “thousands” of drivers lost personal and driver’s license information, with the stolen data including driver’s licenses of 2,567 individuals in Massachusetts, 3,430 people across South Carolina, and 1,873 residents of Rhode Island.
More drivers in Illinois and California, and possibly elsewhere, may also be affected - but these figures are so far unconfirmed.

While Uber did not say which of its third-party service providers got hacked, the media uncovered it was a company called Fireworks AI which, itself, was also a victim of a third-party supply chain attack. Fireworks is a US-based AI infrastructure company that helps businesses deploy and run AI models at scale. Apparently, it provides access to hundreds of AI models, as well as the computing resources needed to run them, and its clients include heavy-hitters such as Shopify, DoorDash, and Notion.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!

Fireworks recently issued a notice saying it spotted a threat actor using internal company credentials to access “environment variables used in evaluation jobs” in a “limited number” of customer accounts.

At first, the company said it did not find evidence of unauthorized access to customer models, datasets, training data, personal information, or inference traffic, but a subsequent update changed the wording somewhat: “At the time of publishing the bulletin, only Fireworks stored secrets (e.g. used in evaluation jobs) were known to have been accessed. Since then, we discovered impacts to account and billing information. For a limited set of accounts, we also discovered impact to secrets, datasets, and incomplete models,” it said.
LLMjacking
The data stolen from Uber seems like added value, not the primary target, as Fireworks says all evidence indicates this was an LLMjacking attack.

LLMjacking is a relatively new term. Google’s Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) recently described it as “the monetization and resource-hijacking of foundation models, which actors achieve through token proxying, automated model streaming, and GPU hardware provisioning.” In other words, someone else is using your AI subscription while you get the bill.

The attacks are quite disruptive, too. Unlike cryptojacking, which takes a long time to rake up any meaningful bills, LLMjacking costs can go up in mere minutes. Google’s recent report showed how a Chinese actor tracked as UNC6993 cost its victims more than $100,000.

The company suffered a secondary attack, as well, less than a month later. On October 23, someone broke into a third-party cloud provider that hosted the company’s R&D machines and used it to reach Fireworks development machines.

There, they ran unauthorized workloads “that led to additional customer data impact.” The attack was spotted on the same day and stopped. “As of October 25, we have not detected further evidence of successful unauthorized access by the threat actor on the Fireworks platform customers use,” the company concluded.
Both Fireworks and Uber are now notifying affected individuals of the breach, and the latter is also offering free identity theft and credit monitoring through Cyberscout.

articles.headline: Anatomy of a blowout
keyFacts: Democrats captured the House majority with around 260 seats and flipped nine seats to win the Senate majority.
A Republican pollster reported that one-third of Trump voters stayed home in 2026 compared to 23 percent of Harris voters.
Independent voters broke heavily for Democrats, shifting seven Senate seats in states Donald Trump won by double digits in 2024.
body: In my final pre- election big-picture analysis column , I ran through some of the ominous signs about what was brewing for the GOP , warning that the so-called fundamentals were dreadful for the incumbent party. There were possibly hopeful indicators, too, but those relied on certain factors breaking Republicans’ way.

Needless to say, the quasi-optimistic scenario never materialized. I wrote, “if things go south on election night for the GOP, with cascading losses piling up as the evening progresses, no one should pretend to be surprised by that potential-to-probable outcome. The writing would have been graffitied all over the proverbial wall.”
Indeed. And what ensued wasn’t merely a blue wave; it was a stunning tsunami. Voters vaulted Democrats from minority status to a dominant House majority, in the neighborhood of 260 seats.

Senate Democrats gained the requisite four seats to capture the upper chamber’s majority — plus five more . In flipping nine seats, they beat formidable candidates (like Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME) and Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-IA)) and weak ones (like Darline Graham, Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-MS), and Ken Paxton) alike.
Everything went wrong. A meltdown of that magnitude required a perfect storm of compounding elements, which is precisely what happened:

Weak GOP turnout: The vice president’s controversial postmortem analysis notwithstanding (he wrote the day after the election that “ our voters did show up ”), vast numbers of Trump supporters and Republican-leaning voters did not participate in this election. Here’s a Republican pollster demonstrating that reality with data:

A third of Trump voters stayed home in 2026. only 23% of Harris voters stayed home in 2026. That’s the story of the midterm. Dem voters were activated, GOP voters weren’t. The conversation should be about why GOP voters stayed home. https://t.co/fkmksmPJGP
— Titus Bond (@TitusBond) November 13, 2026
Yes, some erstwhile Trump backers switched over to back Democrats this time around, but that was a relatively rare phenomenon. The bigger story, by far, was reddish voters staying home:
“8 in 9 Trump voters who didn’t vote GOP stayed home.” https://t.co/CSzEt5bFPF
— Laura Rozen (@lrozen) November 6, 2026

Very strong Democratic turnout: As the first chart above illustrates, Democrats nearly equaled their 2024 House “popular” vote total this year. That’s presidential cycle-level turnout, but in a midterm setting. Meanwhile, the GOP’s cumulative House vote total settled back down to levels similar to 2022. That’s a canyon.
Independents breaking blue, hard: The previous two bullet points (two and a half if you take Republican “flippers” into account) would have yielded a very good overall electoral result for Democrats.

But it took one more data point to turbocharge the wave into something of sufficient magnitude to shift seven Senate seats in states carried by Trump by double digits in 2024 into the Democratic column. That final coup de grace was delivered by independent voters:

Enormous D participation/intensity + massive R voter disengagement + indies going lopsidedly blue were the ingredients for a tsunami, and it happened. https://t.co/nY6E3MU2CJ pic.twitter.com/GiEIthEvlA
— Guy Benson (@guypbenson) November 13, 2026
AN EARLY RUBIO POLL BOUNCE
The really big wave years are easy to spot on this graph, in both directions. And this spread among independents was even larger than in previous wipeout years (1994, 2006, 2010).
Hence, history was made. And Republicans have dug themselves quite a hole.

articles.headline: Grammy Awards: Raye and Rosalia lead nominations
keyFacts: British singer Raye led the Grammy Award nominations on Monday with 11 nods, tying Beyoncé's record for a female artist.
Bruno Mars was the only male artist nominated for Best Album, while BTS declined to submit music in protest.
Grammy winners will be selected by Recording Academy members and announced during a live broadcast on February 7.
body: British singer Raye, with the genre mixing hit "Where Is My Husband!," landed at the top of the list of Grammy Award nominees on Monday, followed by Spanish musician Rosalia and "Choosin" Texas" artist Ella Langley.
Raye earned 11 Grammy nominations including nods for song and record of the year for "Husband," and for album of the year for "This Music May Contain Hope."
She now ties Beyonce's record at the 2025 Grammys for the most nominations in a single year by a female artist.
For her part, Rosalia received nine nominations, just days after sweeping the Latin Grammys with her album "Lux."
First-time nominee Langley secured seven, as did Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers.
Megastar Taylor Swift received five nominations.
Only one male artist nominated for Best Album

Besides Raye, competitors in the album race include Taylor Swift's "The Life of a Showgirl," Langley's "Dandelion," Rosalia's "Lux," Bridgers' "Lost Weekend," Olivia Dean's "The Art of Loving," and Rodrigo's "you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love." Bruno Mars was the only male artist nominated in the category, for his album "The Romantic."

The record of the year category is made up of Dean's “Man I Need,” Langley's “Choosin' Texas,” Mars' “I Just Might,” Raye's “Where Is My Husband!”, Rodrigo's “The Cure,” Rosalía’s “Berghain” featuring Björk and Yves Tumor, Swift's “The Fate of Ophelia” and Tame Impala and Jennie's “Dracula.”

K-pop sensation BTS declined to submit any music for consideration in protest over a new Asian pop music category. Members of the South Korean band said they did not believe music should be categorized by region.
Dolly Parton, the country legend who died in August, received three posthumous nominations.
Winners will be announced on February
The final Grammy voting round will run from December 10 to January 7, with winners selected by around 16,000 Recording Academy members.
Winners will be announced at a red-carpet ceremony in downtown Los Angeles on February 7.
The event will be broadcast live on Walt Disney's ABC and streamed on Disney+ and Hulu.

articles.headline: British actor Robert Pattinson named as new James Bond
keyFacts: Amazon MGM Studios has named Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond, succeeding Daniel Craig as the seventh actor to play 007.
The upcoming movie will be the first Bond film since Amazon took creative control of the franchise.
Reports suggested that Pattinson has signed a commitment to make three Bond films.
body: Robert Pattinson has been named the new James Bond, becoming the seventh actor to assume the role of the iconic British secret agent.

Amazon MGM Studios released a photo of Pattinson in Bond’s signature tuxedo on Monday, confirming the much-anticipated news of who will succeed Daniel Craig. “Identity confirmed,” read a statement posted on Instagram.
Pattinson expressed his gratitude to those at the studio, describing the role as a “dream come true” in a statement.
“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” he added.
The prolonged casting process to replace Craig, who starred as the super-suave spy in five films since 2006, included British actors Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden.

Pattinson shot to international fame playing Edward Cullen in the Twilight series. Since then, he has taken on more independent and fringe roles, most recently in Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime, which starred Pattinson as Chris Hansen from the reality television series To Catch a Predator.

Pattinson has also starred alongside Hollywood superstars Matt Damon and Anne Hathaway in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, as well as Matt Reeves’s The Batman. His film, The Drama, alongside co-star Zendaya, was also released this year.

Pattinson’s debut as Bond, currently untitled but widely referred to as “Bond 26,” will be the first 007 film since long-term producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael Wilson stepped back and Amazon took creative control of the franchise, after acquiring the series’ parent company MGM.
Reports have suggested that Pattinson has signed a commitment to make three Bond films.

articles.headline: Trump backs return of ex-Nvidia boss after 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign launched
keyFacts: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia chief executive after two affairs, but President Donald Trump and tech leaders called for his reinstatement.
Over 175,000 supporters backed Huang's return as the scandal erased hundreds of billions of pounds from Nvidia's market value.
Huang agreed to testify before Congress while Nvidia and the FBI conduct investigations regarding national security concerns.
body: - Published
US President Donald Trump has said he "would certainly not mind" seeing Jensen Huang handed back his job as allies of the former Nvidia chief executive called for him to be reinstated.
Huang resigned as boss of the AI chip giant last week after the emergence of two affairs, one of which was with a woman suspected of spying for China and another allegedly with one of his employees.
It has created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms, which is a key part of the AI industry and its huge expansion.
But now fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have backed a campaign to get Nvidia's board to "Bring Jensen Back".
The pair were among more than 175,000 signatories of an open letter calling for the board to reinstate Huang while an ongoing internal probe is conducted.
President Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back.
"I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he left the White House.

The president's comments come after the "Stand with Jensen" campaign group, which claims to be made up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, demanded the return of the former chief executive.
They expressed concerns the ex-Nvidia boss "was removed without meaningful due process".
Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy.
However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him.

The scandal-hit tech boss is now discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times, external, though the publication reported Nvidia's board is not considering reappointing him.
A representative for Jensen Huang declined to comment on the report. The BBC has contacted Nvidia for comment.
The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House.
President Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal broke out, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy".
Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company.

The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy.
It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.
'China plays games with us, so we play games with China'
On Monday, Trump said he did not know whether the women Huang had an affair with was a spy for China.
"They say she's a spy. I don't know that she was a spy at all. I mean, I really don't, I don't know that." he said.

The Trump administration issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres on Monday, which allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train AI models ahead of Trump's meeting with China President Xi Jingping.

The new rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted.
Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair.
Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said.
The BBC understands that the likelihood of Huang being reinstated is low while Nvidia's internal investigations are ongoing.
The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump.
'A handshake with Jensen'
Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation.
"Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X., external
"Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."
Fellow tech boss Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, sidestepped the question of Huang returning to Nvidia at a conference, saying: "I don't think I know enough to answer that question."
But Altman, who himself was reinstated to his job after being fired back in 2023, said Huang was a "hero of mine".
Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm.
Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading.

In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang".

Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation.
For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Trump defends commerce secretary Lutnick for allegedly slow-walking Nvidia chip export restrictions – live
keyFacts: Donald Trump defended Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick after Lutnick faced criticism for allegedly delaying Nvidia chip export restrictions to China.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is set to testify before Congress about delays in blacklisting Singapore-based company Megaspeed.
Nvidia's board is reportedly not considering bringing back ousted CEO Jensen Huang, despite calls from Donald Trump for his reinstatement.
body: Trump defends under-fire commerce secretary after allegedly slow-walking export restrictions on advanced AI chips

Donald Trump also defended his commerce secretary Howard Lutnick today, after he came under fire for allegedly slow-walking export restrictions on Nvidia chips to China. This comes after the company’s CEO, Jensen Huang, was ousted from his role following a revelation that he had a close relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), allegedly a Chinese operation.

Lutnick is now set to testify before Congress about delays by the commerce department in adding Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is associated with Alice Huang and has bought billions of dollars of Nvidia chips in recent years, to Washington’s blacklist of companies that the US considers a risk to national security despite reported concerns within the administration.

Today, Trump justified any delayed action by Lutnick. “If you didn’t delay it, if you did do something, you could have a blow up with China. We’re having a very good relationship with China right now,” Trump said.
Lutnick is currently traveling with the president and other senior officials and cabinet members to Manila.

Meanwhile, Scott Bessent, Trump’s treasury secretary, said that he has “for months” been in favor of putting Megaspeed on the blacklist – but Lutnick’s commerce department “has the pen”, in an interview with CNBC last week.
“You will have to ask them about their internal process,” he added on Friday.
Nvidia's board not considering bringing back Jensen Huang – reports
As Donald Trump and tech leaders clamor for his return as Nvidia’s CEO, the company’s board of directors is reportedly not considering bringing back Jensen Huang.

The board is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back, CNBC reports this morning, citing a person familiar with the matter. Reuters hears the same, also citing a person familiar.
Huang resigned on Thursday after reports that he had at least two extramarital affairs, one with a woman accused of spying for China and another with a subordinate.

Elon Musk and other tech bosses have called for Huang’s reinstatement, amid reports the AI figurehead is already plotting a return to the chip company, just days after he was ousted. An open letter that has more than 165,000 signatories demands that the company’s board members “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”.

The secluded island of Ni‘ihau has long been a Republican stronghold in deep blue Hawai‘i. Ni‘ihauans have an unusual tendency to unanimously support conservative candidates, like in 2020, when all 43 Ni‘ihauan voters cast their ballots for Donald Trump.

This has been the case since as far back as the early 1900s, when Ni‘ihau’s ballots were sometimes relayed to the neighboring island of Kaua‘i via carrier pigeon. The headline of one characteristic 1939 Honolulu Star Bulletin article reads – “Ni‘ihau Casts 59 Votes All For GOP as Usual.” Bush beat Kerry 39-0, Reagan beat Carter 56-1, and Nixon beat Kennedy 99-0.

But this month, for the first time in recent memory, the island backed a Democrat for governor, casting 14 of their 21 votes for governor Josh Green and lieutenant governor Derek Kawakami. Has Ni‘ihau been caught up in the blue tsunami?
Donald Trump’s efforts to blame Friday’s four-hour nationwide flight stoppage – and the resulting travel chaos – on Democrats are “absurd”, an incoming Democratic member of Congress said yesterday.

The president remained largely silent and out of public view as air travel shut down on Friday, but yesterday he emerged to issue a series of posts blaming the incident on the Biden administration, despite Trump being in office for the last two years in which time Republicans have had control of Congress. He has continued this blame game today (see our earlier post).
Dan Koh, a US House representative-elect from Massachusetts and former Biden administration official, blasted the effort to cast aside blame.

“It’s kind of revisionist history – you might as well start blaming Ronald Reagan for the FAA strike in the 80s as part of this, too,” he said yesterday during an appearance on MS NOW’s The Weekend. “It’s absurd.”

Koh said Joe Bidensecured “historic funding not only to the FAA but over a trillion dollars of infrastructure money” between Trump’s two presidencies. But, Koh added, “a lot of it … Donald Trump has reversed on the grounds of it being too woke”, invoking a term that those on the political right use to refer to things they perceive to be overly leftist.

The congressman-elect said he talks frequently with mayors and city council members in his district about “all this money that would help them with upgrades to transportation including flights” – but “they don’t even know if they’re going to get any more because the [Trump] administration has not even gotten back to them on the status.” He added:
This is the reality: Donald Trump likes to say it’s Biden’s fault, but it’s actually his policies that are stopping the funding from hitting the towns and cities.

Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, announced on Monday that he was disbanding a controversial city police unit that has faced criticism over the years from civil rights groups who have accused the unit of using excessive force and unduly aggressive tactics against protesters.

In a video released on Monday morning, Mamdani said the move stemmed from a campaign pledge he made to disband the New York City police department’s strategic response group (SRG). “Today, we are keeping that promise,” Mamdani said in the video.

An accompanying joint statement from Mamdani and NYPD commissioner Jessica Tisch said the overhaul would “transform how the city prepares for and responds to protests, placing communication, de-escalation and civilian coordination at the center of our approach, while protecting New Yorkers’ constitutional right to protest”.

Along with eliminating the SRG, which was founded in 2015 ostensibly to focus on counter-terrorism, Mamdani and Tisch’s statement also said that the city planned to establish a “first-of-its-kind, civilian-led Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division (CDDD)” within the mayor’s office of community safety.
That division will not have weapons or arrest powers, unlike the SRG, according to the announcement.

The city will also establish what they described as a “specialized dialogue team” that will be known as the “First Amendment Support Team” (Fast) within the NYPD’s community affairs bureau, Mamdani and Tisch’s statement said. The creation of Fast is meant to “improve the NYPD’s protest response”, and it will consist of 30 uniformed officers trained in communication and de-escalation, the mayor and police commissioner said.

Donald Trump said today that he would not mind seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as the chief executive officer of Nvidia.
Trump is speaking to reporters now, ahead of his trip to Manila to attend the Asean summit.
The president added that the suggestion that Huang could return to Nvidia is not a bad idea. He says the ex-CEO has learned a lesson, and denies that national security has been put at risk.
“I think having Jensen go back – a lot of people are asking Jensen - they think Jensen should go back. That certainly isn’t a bad idea,” the president said.
That’s quite an intervention, as an open letter circulates calling for the chip giant to reinstate Huang.

An open letter that has more than 165,000 signatories demands that the company’s board members “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”.

Huang’s resignation on Thursday ended a 33-year run at the helm of the AI company he co-founded, after reports he had at least two extramarital affairs, one with a woman accused of spying for China and another with a subordinate.

According to the Financial Times, Huang has discussed a possible return to the company with people close to him. One Huang ally told the paper they were putting together a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia CEO’s return and would try to garner support from the White House.
“Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” the person said, adding that the efforts had Huang’s support.

The US president will meet his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, for their first trilateral summit, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) forum in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. Before that, he will land in Manila in the Philippines on Tuesday for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit.
At the Asean summit, Trump is expected to sign a trade agreement with Thailand, push deals with other countries and lobby fellow leaders to favour the US over China on artificial intelligence.
He will also take part in the first leaders’ meeting of the Quad partnership – consisting of the US, Japan, India and Australia – since he returned to the White House in January 2025.

White House officials said the president would be accompanied to Apec by Elon Musk, the Tesla and SpaceX entrepreneur who spent almost $500m (£380m) unsuccessfully supporting Republican candidates in this month’s midterms. The reason for Musk’s presence has not been explained.

The China leg of the trip will take place amid the continuing fallout from the Nvidia spying scandal, which prompted the company’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, to resign amid revelations he had had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Trump is under pressure to raise the matter with Xi when they hold a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of Apec.

articles.headline: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
keyFacts: U.N. negotiations are underway in Geneva to consider rules governing lethal autonomous weapons, also known as killer robots.
