body: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
GENEVA — Negotiations on possible rules for the use of lethal autonomous weapons, also known as 'killer robots' are underway at the United Nations in Geneva.

Supporters of controls on autonomous weapons say this week's U.N. conference on Certain Conventional Weapons (or CCW), which meets just once every five years, is the last best chance to agree rules before it is too late.

Warfare technology has advanced rapidly in the last few years, with some experts warning that the world is just months away from having weapons that can choose targets and make the decision to kill autonomously.

In Ukraine and Gaza, AI-assisted weapons have already been used to take out targets, with Ukrainian civilians reporting being 'hunted' by drones as they shop or go to school. But these are still controlled remotely by humans.

Humanitarian organizations say the decision to kill – and responsibility for that choice – must stay in human hands. Ahead of this week's meeting, the United Nations, the International Committee of the Red Cross and the Pope have all called for legally binding rules. U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that allowing fully autonomous weapons to kill would be 'crossing a moral red line'.
What are the risks?

The Red Cross is especially worried that existing rules of war – the Geneva Conventions – cannot be fully respected by autonomous weapons. War is often chaotic and confusing, and the situation can change rapidly. Under the Conventions, soldiers who are wounded or in the process of surrendering can no longer be targeted.

Georgia Haines, a legal adviser with the Red Cross, worries that autonomous weapons will not be able to distinguish between a soldier who is still fighting, one who is wounded and one who wants to surrender.

'The risk is that, based on the technology we are seeing, they are not able to understand in the same way that a human is the contextual signals. And so the risks are incredibly high that there will be a misidentification of a target.'

Meanwhile, human rights groups warn that the technology behind AI-assisted weapons is becoming increasingly cheap and easy to use. The more it is adopted by the military, the greater the danger of proliferation and its use by terrorist groups or law enforcement agencies in repressive regimes. In theory, a swarm of autonomous drones could be programmed to kill everyone wearing a red sweater, everyone carrying a poster or even everyone speaking a certain language.

Many of the countries now meeting in Geneva take such concerns very seriously. At least 50, including Ireland, Italy, Brazil, Mexico, France and Germany, are calling for a strict timetable to agree on binding rules governing autonomous weapons.

But among states that are already developing and using semi-autonomous weapons, there is pushback. The United States, Russia and Israel have indicated they are set to oppose legally binding rules, with Washington proposing a five-year timetable to draft non-binding guidelines instead.

The U.S. is traditionally a late adopter of international treaties. It did not ratify the Ottawa Convention on landmines, for example, although it did, over time, stop deploying them and reduce its stockpiles.

Under President Trump, doubts about international law have grown. Washington has imposed sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court, and just this weekend, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in a keynote speech to the Federalist Society, warned against "quoting laws to men with swords."

The problem for states meeting in Geneva is that U.N. negotiations on limiting specific weapons are supposed to be conducted by consensus. This was achieved in 1995, when countries agreed to a ban on blinding lasers, but other agreements have proved elusive. With landmines, countries frustrated by the delay finally took negotiations outside the U.N. process to create the Ottawa Convention.

This week, there may be a compromise: a longer or even open-ended negotiating period to come up with rules that individual states can adopt as binding or non-binding. For diplomats supporting such a solution, it is a way to ensure at least some progress. For campaigners, it is less than ideal, with one likening it to kicking a very dangerous can down the road.

articles.headline: I installed a GTA 5 drag racing mod that got derailed by my roving band of hitmen mod
keyFacts: A PC Gamer writer installed the Drag Meets mod for Grand Theft Auto 5, which includes social simulation elements.
The drag racing event was disrupted before it could begin because an airborne minivan filled with hitmen attacked the participants.
Lamar shot back at the attackers, causing chaos that killed the racers and teleported the player to the airport.
body: I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

Look, I'll be real with you. When I installed Drag Meets – Quick n Dirty Edition, I was not expecting it to go well. Cars spend most of their time flying and exploding in my copy of Grand Theft Auto 5, and these circumstances aren't conducive to gentlemanly racing.

I didn't anticipate it going quite as badly as it did, though. Drag Meets is actually rather complex: you don't just rock up to an objective marker, tap E, and get warped behind the wheel of a car. There's a lite social sim element to the whole thing, so you walk up to an objective marker, tap E, and suddenly find yourself standing in the midst of a drag racing soirée.

Drag meets are a scene, it turns out, and the scene's members have names, goals, and ambitions. A racer named "Blue Anime Panto" is seeking a challenger, the notifications inform me. "Blade had joined the meet", reads another. A lady called Tempesta has been forced to leave the meet because her engine broke, apparently. How did this happen? Either it's a randomly rolled event or her car flew into the sun; I am unable to tell.

It's not just Tempesta who's leaving the meet. Everyone is leaving, on account of the airborne minivan, just overhead, filled with hitmen determined to kill us all. They should be determined to kill me and only me, but Lamar (from GTA 5, you know? Lamar was also there. Keep up) began shooting back at them and all hell broke loose.

The drag race—if it's even possible—never got the opportunity to start. Pretty soon, racing legends like Stinger GT and Rhapsody were face-down in the Los Santos grass. And then I teleported to the airport.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

One of Josh's first memories is of playing Quake 2 on the family computer when he was much too young to be doing that, and he's been irreparably game-brained ever since. His writing has been featured in Vice, Fanbyte, and the Financial Times. He'll play pretty much anything, and has written far too much on everything from visual novels to Assassin's Creed. articles.headline: Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone
keyFacts: Spry Fox announced Spirit Crossing, a multiplayer hangout game where players appear as shadows until they interact.
The game offers cooperative activities like fishing and crafting, but allows players to remain completely isolated if they prefer.
Developers confirmed they used generative AI tools like Claude for behind-the-scenes tasks such as editing config files.
body: New multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

Deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out together.

There's nothing forcing you to do any of this in company, mind. "Stay a mysterious shadow, lend a hand when you feel like it, and disappear before anyone can make it weird," the devs explain, adding a hug emoji to make plain that they don't think you're some kind of smelly misanthrope for shunning other players.

I, personally, am a smelly misanthrope, and will only ever appear in your game as a skulking opacity, peering through the window of your personal gingerbread house, with its tastefully accessorised lava lamps and throw rugs. No, I will not join you for a group hang-glider tour. No, I do not want to play the banjo with you. You will experience me only as the nagging sensation of being watched, while you chat to the local "Stylesmith" about fetching rucksack patterns.

Spirit Crossing has an upfront cost that "gives players full access to the complete game experience in perpetuity", but you can also take out a subscription for some cosmetic items and access to a "limited resource exchange shop". They're avoiding traditional microtransactions, which is nice.

Spry Fox are also the developers of Cozy Grove - "the best grove since Byker", wrote Graham, in one of his regular 'senior moments'. I myself know them as the studio behind wintry puzzler Road Not Taken, with its randomised woodlands, and block-merging city builder Triple Town, with its unexpectedly terrifying bears. Little about Spirit Crossing seems terrifying, unless you count the shadow loitering at the edge of your conversation pit. Read more on Steam.

Update: Ah, sod it. As has been pointed out to us on Bluesky, Spirit Crossing is sadly among the games that use generative AI tools - specifically, according to various Discord responses from the developers, they've used Anthropic's Claude for behind-the-scenes tasks, such as editing several config files at once. There's no disclosure on the game's Steam page because Spry Fox haven't used AI tools to generate any of the art or music - Valve rewrote Steam's disclosure requirements in January to exempt the usage of generative AI for "efficiency gains", which the above presumably falls under.

articles.headline: Trump brings two divided Cabinet heavyweights to China as controversy hangs over high-stakes talks
keyFacts: President Donald Trump brought Cabinet officials Scott Bessent and Howard Lutnick on an Asia trip despite their dispute over restricting AI chips to China.
Treasury Secretary Bessent said multiple departments supported blacklisting Megaspeed over China AI concerns, but Commerce Secretary Lutnick reportedly resisted.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 regarding Nvidia AI chip exports, CBS reported.
body: President Donald Trump is bringing two powerful Cabinet officials divided over restrictions on China's access to advanced American AI chips on his high-stakes Asia trip, as controversy over the issue follows them into talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick are both accompanying Trump on the four-day trip despite reports of a dispute over whether to blacklist a company suspected of helping China obtain restricted American AI technology. Trump acknowledged their competing views Monday and suggested Lutnick may have delayed action to avoid worsening relations with Beijing.

"He might have delayed it, but he was doing that because you could have if you didn't delay it. If you didn't do something, you could have a blow up with China. We're having a very good relationship with China right now, and I understand both sides of it, and I'll make a decision. But I understand very well both sides," the president said.

The dispute follows reports that Lutnick resisted efforts to place Singapore-based Megaspeed on a U.S. trade blacklist, despite Trump reportedly supporting action against the company on three occasions this year, according to Axios. Megaspeed has faced allegations that its operations helped Chinese companies gain access to restricted Nvidia chips.
TWO TOP TRUMP CABINET OFFICIALS GO TO WAR OVER CHINA SPY SCANDAL AMID EXPLOSIVE ACCUSATIONS: REPORT

The Commerce Department announced a new rule this week aimed at preventing Chinese companies and other restricted foreign entities from accessing advanced American computing technology through data centers in third countries. The department said the rule was written at the direction of the Treasury Department and National Security Council.
Trump told reporters Monday he is not considering replacing Lutnick, saying "he's done a very good job."

Bessent publicly confirmed Friday that several administration departments had supported adding Megaspeed to the Commerce Department's Entity List, which would restrict the company's access to U.S. technology.
"Treasury, War, USTR and State — they were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the Entity List for months, but Commerce has the pen," Bessent said.
The Commerce Department denied Axios' account of a confrontation between Bessent and Lutnick in the White House Situation Room, saying the two officials had no such conversation.
Trump is bringing several of his administration's most powerful officials on the four-day Asia trip, which includes stops in the Philippines and China.
TRUMP TO CONFRONT XI AT HIGH-STAKES SUMMIT OVER CHINA BACKING FOR IRAN, RUSSIA

The delegation includes Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Bessent, Lutnick, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett, among other officials, a White House official confirmed to Fox News Digital.

Trump is expected to meet with world leaders, participate in regional economic and security summits and hold high-stakes talks with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin, and possibly North Korea leader Kim Jong Un.

The controversy has also drawn attention to Nvidia's leadership . Nvidia announced Thursday that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned following reports about his relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for China.
Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing and said Sunday that it retained outside counsel to investigate allegations surrounding its operations.
Trump said Monday it has not been confirmed she is a spy.
FEDERAL PROSECUTOR WARNS SEN WARREN OF 'LEGAL CONSEQUENCES' IF RECORDS AREN'T PRESERVED IN TRUMP-LINKED PROBES

Lutnick, the former chairman and CEO of investment firm Cantor Fitzgerald, is one of the wealthiest officials to serve in a presidential administration. A longtime Trump ally, he co-chaired the president's 2024 transition team, and the two have known each other for decades through New York's business and social circles.
Lutnick has also agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 amid growing scrutiny of the Commerce Department's handling of Nvidia chip exports to China, CBS News reported.

Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Chris Coons, D-Del., jointly called on the administration to preserve records related to Nvidia's advanced AI chip exports and potential national security risks. The senators set a Nov. 17 deadline for written confirmation that the records would be preserved and requested a congressional briefing.

articles.headline: Your Samsung phone could soon get a personal AI agent – what we know about Galaxy Claw
keyFacts: Samsung is reportedly developing an AI upgrade called Galaxy Claw to give Galaxy AI cross-app functionality.
Android Authority reported that Galaxy Claw uses Personal Agent Core to access compatible apps like Contacts and Messages.
Reports say Samsung is testing subscriptions for heavy Galaxy AI users, which might incur a fee.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- Samsung is reportedly working on an AI upgrade called Galaxy Claw.
- The upgrade appears to give Galaxy AI cross-app functionality.
- Samsung is considering subscriptions for frequent Galaxy AI users.

Samsung’s Galaxy AI may be getting a cross-app intelligence upgrade, à la Google’s Gemini Intelligence and Apple’s Siri AI, according to an Android Authority report. Samsung is working on Galaxy Claw, which could make Galaxy AI more agentic and context-aware across your apps.

Currently, Galaxy AI lives inside your Galaxy devices and apps, but its smarts are limited to the apps it’s integrated with. Android Authority reports that Samsung’s Personal Agent Core is at the center of Galaxy Claw, connecting Galaxy AI to compatible apps and services, such as Calendar, Contacts, Messages, Gmail, Gallery, Phone, and Voice Recorder.
More from ZDNET

Android Authority found code that referred to Galaxy Claw in Samsung’s Personal Agent Core app, suggesting that Galaxy AI can complete cross-app tasks. For example, take the request: “Remind me to buy Mom a birthday card two days before her birthday.” An assistant without access to multiple apps will set a reminder to buy Mom a birthday card, but you might have to manually enter the date and time for the reminder to notify you.

With a more agentic assistant, it can access Mom’s contact card and her birthdate, calculate two days before her birthday, and remind you on that date. Like Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI, Personal Agent Core will need special permissions to access your sensitive information, such as messages, photos, and calls.

Android Authority also reports that code strings in the app point to a recurring, scheduled tasks feature, which would allow users to create custom automations and determine how often Galaxy AI should execute them, similar to Apple’s revamped Shortcuts.

Other code strings reveal a Daily Brief, Device Cleaner, Travel Planner, and a widget. An AI-powered daily brief is something I’ve been yearning for as an iPhone user. If I want a Siri-created brief, I’d have to build it via Shortcuts.

Gmail features a Gemini-powered daily brief, which compiles information from my email inbox and GChat messages to show me things I may have missed. I find it very useful for work, since my inbox is flooded and I often miss important emails.

Samsung’s Galaxy ecosystem includes smartphones, smartwatches, smart rings, earbuds, and tablets, so there are plenty of opportunities for a more agentic Galaxy AI to bridge gaps across the devices in your personal ecosystem.

Additionally, Google Gemini integration is sweeping across Android (and iOS) apps, which might prompt Galaxy users to choose the more robust AI assistant over Galaxy AI. If Samsung can find ways to make Galaxy AI more useful and exclusive to Galaxy users, it might win some people over. However, reports say Samsung is testing subscriptions for heavy Galaxy AI users, so more Galaxy AI integration might incur a fee.

body: Democratic pundit James Carville got defensive when former CNN anchor and podcaster Don Lemon brought up Florida democratic socialist Angie Nixon’s recent claim that Carville is racist and needs to retire.

“This is what Angie Nixon said about you,” Lemon shared with Carville on his show over the weekend. “She said, ‘The man is a racist.’ She said, ‘The way in which he talks and how he has continued to downplay the work that I was able to do, and the work that other folks have been able to do, other Black candidates, is just really mad disrespectful.’”

Carville had bashed Nixon as “a uniquely uninspiring Senate candidate” and “not a good fit for the state of Florida” during her run for U.S. Senate, which she lost to Republican incumbent Ashley Moody this month.
Lemon told Carville that Nixon had said he “needs to go retire and stop being disrespectful.”
“Who needs to go retire?” Carville asked irritably.
“She’s talking about you ― she said that you’re racist,” Lemon answered.

“Yeah, ask Val Demings. Ask Cheri Beasley. Ask Scott Colom,” Carville said, engaging in the old “I have Black friends” defense by listing Black candidates he’s supported. “That’s the easiest thing in the world to just pop off and call anybody a racist. I’m bothered by that not at all.”
“Again, she can call Val, who ran for the Senate before. I don’t know how many fundraising appeals I’ve had, but that’s fine,” he added. “I’m 82 years old. Call me whatever you want.”
Nixon called out Carville directly during an appearance on “The Joy Reid Show” last week.

“It doesn’t matter if you don’t like me,” she said of the pundit. “I didn’t drag anyone down.” She added that her campaign was able to turn out people who were not historic midterm voters and questioned his expertise.
“James Carville, your analysis is wack,” she said. “It is not truthful, and it is rooted in the white supremacy that continues to run this country.”

articles.headline: New NIAID director will pivot agency away from ‘mad science experiments’ of Anthony Fauci: Jay Bhattacharya
keyFacts: NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya is appointing John Powers as NIAID director to shift the agency away from biodefense research toward basic immunology.
The Department of War will now handle NIAID's biodefense research programs, which previously received over $2.2 billion of the agency's budget.
Bhattacharya said NIAID will focus on common infectious diseases, while Powers stated the agency will support research rather than set policy.
body: WASHINGTON — National Institutes of Health Director Jay Bhattacharya will elevate the interim head of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases to become its new director on Monday, in a pivot away from biodefense research and back to immunology basics.

Bhattacharya is appointing John Powers — a 20-year veteran of NIAID and its fourth director in the last four years — to usher in a new era at the agency that will end what he bluntly dubbed the “mad science experiments” of ex-director Anthony Fauci.

Fauci ran NIAID for 40 years and had great success in developing life-saving treatments for HIV as well as running the biodefense and emerging infectious disease research that soon took up the largest portion of its annual budget.

“There’s a strict adherence to the work to make sure that it doesn’t — we don’t — conduct, you know, just bluntly, mad science experiments,” Bhattacharya told The Post in an interview Friday. “No more dangerous gain of function will happen under John’s leadership.”

Focus on taxpayer funding for that research heightened during the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to fierce debates in Congress between Fauci and lawmakers over its role in possibly creating the virus that causes SARS-CoV-2.
As recently as fiscal year 2025, roughly one-third of NIAID’s budget, or more than $2.2 billion, was for biodefense research programs, which now will be run by the Department of War.
“We’re now purely a civilian agency,” Bhattacharya also affirmed. “We’re moving to shift the portfolio so it’s more balanced toward infectious diseases that Americans actually get.”

Powers added that, in his earlier years as a clinician, “I was there when HIV patients were dying. And we made tremendous progress in that area. But right now we’re able to send HIV patients home with one pill once a day. And we’re focusing much more now on implementation research, which means we’re trying to get interventions to people who really need it.”

As a result, Bhattacharya and Powers said they have combed through more than 8,000 research grants to ensure that none of the lab work involved dangerous experiments that would be classified as biodefense.

“Biodefense is research to go find emerging diseases in the middle of nowhere, bring them into labs, make them more transmissible, make them more able to infect humans and then develop sort of hypothetical … poorly tested countermeasures to pretend like we can address them if they if they happen to emerge,” Bhattacharya explained. “We’re out of that business altogether.”

“There were civilian justifications, but those justifications were far-fetched, right? The idea that we could prepare for all pathogens out there — they’re literally in the trillions — and somehow develop countermeasures for all the most important ones by making them more pathogenic,” he added.

Fauci has repeatedly denied in congressional testimony that his agency ever funded such experiments at the Wuhan Institute of Virology, located in the city where COVID-19 emerged in late 2019 — though Bhattacharya and other scientists have disputed this claim or said it is impossible to know what Chinese scientists were researching under the US-funded grant.

As the face of the US public health response to COVID, Fauci further denounced all his critics by claiming they were sowing distrust about science itself — “because I represent science” — but his private diary entries showed him expressing uncertainty about natural spillover theories.

Emails uncovered through congressional investigations also revealed that Fauci operated a “secret back channel” with his senior adviser, David Morens, as the latter was trying to get the grant for research at the WIV reinstated.

In June 2024 congressional testimony, Fauci disavowed Morens, saying he “knew nothing” of the alleged use of a private Gmail account to discuss official government grants — which also involved purported kickbacks — and claimed he wasn’t even his adviser.

Morens has since pleaded guilty in August to charges of concealing federal records about those grants, which are critical to discovering the true origin of COVID-19. The month before, Fauci took the Fifth Amendment more than 100 times in congressional testimony to avoid questioning.
“What happened in the pandemic … didn’t feel like science to me,” Bhattacharya said, adding that Fauci’s actions were at “the root of a lot of the distrust that Americans have over the NIH.”
“It felt like a perversion of science that focused more on power, rather than on truth,” he added.
That also included heavy redactions from NIH officials to records requests made by journalists, scientists and the American public.
“We’ve been working closely with Congress in delivering a whole bunch of records from that era,” Bhattacharya also said.
Powers noted that the shift in focus at NIAID would also move it away from “setting policy,” another point of disagreement during the pandemic.

“As a practicing physician, I think there’s still some outstanding questions that remain to be addressed about things like masks,” he said. “Our job is to actually help support the research that would answer those questions.”
“But our job is not to tell everybody what to do,” he added. “Our job is to provide them with the information to make the best decisions.”

keyFacts: Retailers are offering discounts on PlayStation 5 hardware ahead of Black Friday, including $20 off DualSense controllers and $30 off the DualSense Edge.
New PlayStation 5 consoles are currently excluded from the discounts due to rising component costs and the upcoming launch of Grand Theft Auto VI.
Additional hardware deals include price cuts on Sony's 27-inch gaming monitor, wireless headsets, earbuds, and console covers.
body: Several retailers are offering discounts on PlayStation 5 games, including deep price cuts on recent console-exclusive hits like Marvel’s Wolverine , Ghost of Yotei , Saros , and hundreds more. We’ll cover a bunch of those in the coming days, but this post is focused on the great hardware discounts that are happening, including $20 off the stellar DualSense wireless controller and its many color schemes, as well as $30 off the customizable DualSense Edge . The big sale also extends to headsets , console covers , and even Sony’s 27-inch monitor that has a hook to charge your controller.

Sitting out from the discounts, at least for now, are new PlayStation 5 consoles. It’s not impossible that a deal will surface later this month, though it’s more unlikely to happen than in past years for a couple of reasons. For one, console deals are exceedingly rare due to the rise in costs for the consoles associated with RAMageddon. Perhaps the bigger reason is Grand Theft Auto VI , a system-selling game launching November 19th that will likely convince a lot of people to pay full price for a console. Not to worry, though. We’ve included a link below for Sony-refurbished consoles that are cheaper than buying new.
Here are some of the best hardware-related deals we’ve seen from Sony’s PlayStation Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals.
Sony PlayStation 27-inch 1440p gaming monitor
The 1440p 240Hz refresh rate screen is sleek, but pretty basic for the price. It stands out, though, thanks to its DualSense-charging cradle that extends from its bottom. This is the first discount.
